title: Lessons 1–3. HTML and CSS basics
description: HTML structure, linking CSS, selectors, cascade and specificity

learn.intro: Hi! Let's review lessons 1–3: **HTML and CSS basics**. I'll explain everything section by section, like teacher {teacher} in class, and after each section there's a short check. Ready?

sections.title: A website is like a living person

slides.text: A person has a skeleton, an appearance (skin, clothes) and a brain. A website also has **3 parts** — and 3 languages we are learning.

**HTML** is the skeleton: the main structure of the site. Without HTML there is no site at all.
**CSS** is skin and clothes: color, font, beauty.
**JavaScript** is the brain: reactions and movement, what happens on click.
Code is a set of commands that a computer and a browser understand. We don't write in ordinary words but by strict rules — using tags.

check.prompt: Match the language and the part of the «person»
You can make a website with no HTML at all — just CSS.
check.explain: HTML is the skeleton. Without it there's no site, and CSS has nothing to «dress».

slides.text: We create the file **index.html**. The `.html` extension is a sign for the browser: «open me as a web page». Write code → **Ctrl + S** → refresh the browser with **F5**.
The base of any page:

`<html>` is the outermost «box».
`<head>` is the page's «passport», it's **not visible**.
`<title>` is the tab name.
`<body>` is everything **visible** on the screen.
Remember: what's inside head is not visible on screen. What's inside body is visible.

check.prompt: Where do you write text that should be visible on the page?
check.explain: Everything inside body is visible on the screen.

check.prompt: Which tag changes the browser tab name? Write it without brackets.
check.explain: title is the heading on the browser tab.

slides.text: A **tag** is a command in HTML. It's written in angle brackets `< >`. Almost every tag is **paired**: opening and closing, the closing one has `/`.

Common tags: `

`…`

You can add a style right in the tag with the **style** attribute — it's the smallest, «by hand» way of CSS:
`color` is the text color (try red, green). `font-size` is the text size (compare 12px and 40px).

check.prompt: Which tag is an image with no closing tag?
check.explain: is an exception: it has no closing tag.

check.prompt: What does color: red change in the style attribute?
check.explain: color is the text color. Background is background-color.

slides.text: **HTML** says **what** is on the page. **CSS** says **how it looks**: red, big, centered.
Imagine two rooms. Room 1 is `index.html` (content). Room 2 is `style.css` (design). And the **door** between them is the `<link>` tag. Without the door, HTML knows nothing about CSS.
We put the door inside `<head>`. `rel="stylesheet"` means «this is a stylesheet», `href="style.css"` — which file we connect to.
If CSS doesn't work — check first: is the file saved (Ctrl + S), is the file name in link spelled correctly, is there a ; at the end of each line.

check.prompt: The style.css file should be in the same folder as index.html.
check.explain: Then it's enough to write just style.css in href.

check.prompt: What does href="style.css" mean in the link tag?
check.explain: href is the file address. «This is a stylesheet» is rel="stylesheet".

slides.text: First we say **who** we style, then **how**:
`p` is the **selector** (who), `{ }` holds the styling, `color` is the **property** (what we change), `blue` is the **value** (what we make it), `;` ends the line.
Rules: in a selector, the tag is written **without** `< >`. Between the property and the value — a colon `:`. At the end of each line — `;`, otherwise the next line may not work.
Size properties: `width` — width, `height` — height, `px` — pixel, the smallest dot on the screen. Tip: add `background-color`, otherwise you can't see the block's edges.

check.prompt: In the rule h1 { font-size: 40px; } match the parts

check.explain: Every line needs a ; at the end. Without it the next line may not work.

slides.text: If you write `p` in CSS, **all** paragraphs change at once. But the 5th one has its own `style`:
Result: all paragraphs are **blue**, and the 5th is **red**. The browser's rule: **a more precise and closer instruction is stronger**.

The teacher told the whole class: «Everyone writes with a blue pen». Then told one student separately: «You write with a red one». That student follows the personal instruction — it was said to them specifically.

check.prompt: The style attribute affects all paragraphs on the page.
check.explain: style affects only one element — the one it is written in.

slides.text: A selector is a way to say exactly **who** to style. If there are 30 people in a room, shouting «put on a hat!» — it's unclear who you mean.
**By tag** `p { }` — all paragraphs. **By class** `.card { }` — all elements with `class="card"`, even if they are different tags. A class is like a «name badge».
An ID is like a passport, it's unique. But in real projects IDs are not used for styles: they are for JavaScript and anchor links. For CSS, always use CLASSES.
**Nesting**: `.card p` is a paragraph that is **inside** `.card`. A paragraph outside doesn't change.

check.prompt: How do you select all elements with class="box"?

options: Only a div with the class card
check.explain: Tag + class together: only a div that has the class card.

slides.text: If two rules «argue» over one element — the **more precise** one wins. Strength hierarchy: **ID > class > tag**.
Here the text will be **red**: `.card p` (class + tag) is more precise than just `p`.

**Order rule**: if the strength is equal, the rule written **lower** in the file wins.
**!important** is the «emergency button»: it always wins, but using it is not recommended.

check.prompt: Two .title rules of equal strength: first color: green, below it color: orange. Which color?
check.explain: With equal strength, the rule written lower wins.

questions.prompt: If we compare a website to a person, HTML is…
questions.explain: HTML is the main structure of the site, its «building». Without HTML there is no site at all.

questions.prompt: Match the language and its role on the site
Everything written inside <head> is visible on the screen.
questions.explain: head is the page's «passport», it's not visible. What's inside body is visible.

questions.prompt: Which tag sets the tab name in the browser?
questions.explain: Change the text in title — and the tab name changes.

questions.prompt: What is the extension of an HTML file? (for example, index.???)
questions.explain: The .html extension tells the browser: «open me as a web page».

questions.prompt: How is a closing tag different from an opening one?
questions.explain:
is opening,

is closing. The / sign shows where the tag ends.

questions.prompt: The tag has no closing tag.
questions.explain: Most tags are paired, but (image) is an exception.

questions.prompt: Which heading is the biggest?
questions.explain: Headings go from h1 to h6, h1 is the biggest.

questions.prompt: Put the tags in the right order, as in the page structure
questions.explain: html is the outer «box». Inside: first head, then body. Every tag is closed.

questions.prompt: What will font-size: 24px do in this tag?
questions.explain: font-size is the letter size. Color is set by color.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the stylesheet file we created in lesson 2?
questions.explain: style.css is «room 2», where the site's design lives.

questions.prompt: Which tag is the «door» between index.html and style.css?
questions.explain: Without <link>, HTML knows nothing about CSS and styles don't work.

questions.prompt: The <link> tag for connecting CSS is written inside <head>.
questions.explain: <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> goes in head.

questions.prompt: In the rule p { color: blue; } match the part and its name
Which CSS is correct?
questions.explain: In a selector the tag has no < >, a colon goes between property and value, and a semicolon at the end.

questions.prompt: If you forget ; at the end of a line, the next CSS line may not work.
questions.explain: A semicolon is required at the end of each line.

questions.prompt: Why add background-color when testing width and height?
options: width doesn't work without a background
questions.explain: Without a background you can't see the block's edges or notice that the size changed.

questions.prompt: How do you target elements with class="card" in CSS?
questions.explain: A class is targeted with a dot: .card. With # — that's an ID.

questions.prompt: What are IDs used for in real projects?
questions.explain: An ID has too high a priority, its style is hard to override. Classes are used for CSS.

questions.prompt: What color will the 5th paragraph be?
questions.code:
Paragraph 4

Paragraph 5

Paragraph 6

/* CSS */ p { color: blue; }
questions.explain: style is written right in the tag — it's a personal instruction, stronger than the general rule p { }.

questions.prompt: Arrange the selectors from strongest to weakest
questions.explain: Strength hierarchy: ID > class > tag.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph will turn green?
questions.code:
I'm inside the card

I'm outside

/* CSS */ .card p { color: green; }
questions.explain: .card p means «a p that is inside .card». The paragraph outside doesn't change.

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.code:
What color will I be?

/* CSS */ p { color: blue; } .card p { color: red; }
questions.explain: .card p (class + tag) is more precise and stronger than just p.

questions.prompt: The selectors have equal strength. What color will the heading be?
questions.code:
Heading

/* CSS */ .title { color: green; } .title { color: orange; }
questions.explain: Order rule: with equal strength, the one written lower (later) wins.

questions.prompt: What color will the text be?
questions.code:
Text

/* CSS */ .card p { color: red; } p { color: blue !important; }
questions.explain: !important is the «emergency button»: it wins even on a weak selector. But using it is not recommended.
